state: <Insert the complete UN input with its three marked sections>

instructions.task: Select the question-generation mode best suited to the TARGET BLOCK: lookup, practitioner, semantic, or skip. Assess the strongest usable information need in the target, not the document as a whole. Do not generate questions or answers.

input_structure.### TARGET BLOCK: The passage that questions must be about. Every answer must be fully stated here.
input_structure.### REFERENCED DOCUMENTS: Documents cited by the target, with symbols, titles, and text. These help interpretation but cannot supply answers.
input_structure.### DOCUMENT CONTEXT: Surrounding passages from the same document. These resolve names, dates, speakers, and situations but cannot supply answers.

instructions.metadata: The target opens with a language tag, document symbol, and title. These help identify the source type, author or organ, date, and subject. Different-language versions represent the same passage. All modes are available for all document types, including resolutions, reports, letters, and PV/SR meeting records.
instructions.source_interpretation: Resolve the actual speaker, reporting source, or responsible body from the target and local context. Do not assume that the chair, sender, recipient, or person named in the title made the target statement. Preserve whether the content is an adopted decision, recommendation, proposal, future commitment, completed action, or attributed assessment. A reported position is not automatically an applicable rule.
usable_content: A mode must support at least one specific, informative question with a short answer fully available in the target. Questions may use supporting material to resolve context, but not to obtain missing answer substance.
A rule merely quoted or restated from another instrument is not the target's own contribution. Consider what this target itself applies, changes, reports, or contests instead.

Exclude ceremony, generic exhortations, and unchanged recurring statements without instance-specific substance. In mixed passages, retain concrete facts, decisions, mechanisms, or assessments; a ceremonial opening does not invalidate every fact that follows.

A year alone does not make generic content distinctive. Look for a specific mission, country, body, measure, event, reporting instance, or other substantive anchor. Do not invent missing distinctions or assume repetition solely because the document belongs to a recurring series.
selection: Assess all three modes before selecting. Prefer the strongest directly supported information need, not the broadest possible wording or the mode expected to receive higher verifier scores.

For precise information, prefer practitioner when the regime, date, and necessary attribution identify the need naturally without a document locator. Prefer lookup when locating the point in a particular source is itself useful. The presence of a document symbol is not evidence that lookup is the better mode.

Prefer semantic when the target directly supports a conceptual question about a concrete situation, response, mechanism, affected party, or stated rationale. Do not turn an isolated datum into a vague how or why question, or treat broad policy language as automatically semantic.

When several modes fit different parts of the target, choose the one supporting the clearest, most specific question with the least forced framing. Precise questions are not inferior merely because they are direct; conceptual questions are not superior merely because they sound broader.

Choose skip only when no mode has usable content. Failure of one mode does not establish the suitability of another. Do not force balanced mode frequencies or favour a mode because of its position in the choices.

lookup.persona: A practitioner knows the source and wants one precise point from it.
lookup.information_need: A measure, deadline, ceiling, criterion, mandate task, reporting arrangement, responsible body, procedure, scope, concrete figure, or attributed finding.
lookup.question_properties: The source is an explicit locator. Two renderings differ only by replacing an accurate dated source description with its official identifier, including a PV/SR symbol when applicable. The subject anchor, necessary attribution, and absolute time remain clear in both renderings.
lookup.fit: Best when source-specific retrieval is natural and both renderings can remain concise and self-contained. A speaker's statement must stay attributed to that speaker's State or office, not become a finding of the meeting body.

practitioner.persona: A specialist knows the regime or operational setting and wants a precise norm or fact at a particular time, without locating a document.
practitioner.information_need: What was required, permitted, covered, due, or operationally established; a condition, exemption, mandate, deadline, ceiling, procedure, or concrete attributed fact or figure.
practitioner.question_properties: The question uses appropriate specialist terminology, an absolute time anchor, and at least two substantive anchors. It does not use an instrument or meeting record as a locator. Attribution to a State or office is allowed for concrete information reported in any document type.
practitioner.fit: Best when the precise information need stands naturally without a document reference. Preserve recommendations as recommendations and reported facts as attributed facts; do not infer binding law or implementation from a speech or proposal.

semantic.persona: A searcher knows the situation but not the governing source or its vocabulary.
semantic.information_need: Situation: a concrete problem, development, assessment, or stated rationale. Response: an action or mechanism and how it operates. Stakeholder: who is bound, protected, or assisted and how, or a State's position on an identifiable proposal or measure.
semantic.question_properties: The question describes the situation in ordinary words while preserving legal terms, official names, attribution, and modality. It has a concrete substantive anchor and an absolute year or date, without document identifiers.
semantic.fit: Best when conceptual framing captures substantive content explicitly present in the target. A figure may support a conceptual assessment, but requesting that figure by name belongs to a precise mode. Generic topics, speech summaries, and unsupported explanations do not qualify.

criteria.skip: No mode supports a specific, informative, directly answerable question about the target. This includes ceremony, generic or unchanged recurring content without a usable fact, unresolved essential attribution, and answer substance available only outside the target. Document type alone never justifies skip.
